title: A Fresh Start for the World

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: This is the account of Shem, Ham and Japheth, Noah's sons, who themselves had sons after the flood. - Gen 10:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This single verse opens one of the most remarkable chapters in the Bible - a family tree that becomes a map of the whole human race. From these three sons of Noah would come every nation on earth. And notice the quiet but important phrase: "after the flood." Life did not end at the flood; it began again. God's purpose for a world full of people flourished once more.

There is real hope here. The flood had been a devastating judgement, seemingly the end of everything. Yet God brought a new beginning out of it. Where we might have expected an empty, silent world, we find instead the beginnings of nations, peoples, and languages spreading across the earth. God is a God of new beginnings, who brings life out of what looked like an ending.

This is the pattern of all God's dealings. He does not abandon His purposes when things fall apart. He preserves a remnant, brings them through, and begins again. What sin and judgement seem to destroy, God's grace restores.

The whole sweep of Scripture moves this way - through judgement to renewal, through death to resurrection. The greatest "after" of all came when Jesus rose from the grave, bringing new creation life to all who trust Him (2 Cor 5:17). Whatever floods lie behind you, God specialises in the "after." He is writing a new account, and His purposes for life and blessing will always outlast the ruins of the past.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you believe God can bring new beginnings after seasons of ruin?
- Where do you need to trust God for an "after" in your life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: God of new beginnings, thank You that You bring life out of endings and hope out of ruins. Help me trust Your purposes when things fall apart, and thank You for the new creation life I have in Christ.
